Row.Text: Yumbu Lagang
Mountain tiles provide Defense Points to Cities. Defense Buildings provide +1 [ICON_PEACE] Faith.[NEWLINE]Must be built on a Mountain.
[NEWLINE]"From the highest peaks, the gods watch over their children below."[NEWLINE] - Tibetan Proverb[NEWLINE]

Yumbu Lagang is considered the first palace in Tibet and holds immense significance as the legendary birthplace of Tibetan civilization. According to tradition, it was built in the 2nd century BCE for the first Tibetan king, Nyatri Tsenpo, who descended from the heavens. Located in the Yarlung Valley in what is now the Shannan Prefecture, the palace sits dramatically atop a hill overlooking the Yarlung River.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The structure represents the earliest example of Tibetan architecture and served as the seat of early Tibetan kings for centuries. Its name translates to "Palace of Mother and Son," reflecting its role in royal succession. The palace's strategic mountain location provided both defensive advantages and symbolic connection to the sacred peaks that Tibetans believe house protective deities. Though destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, it was rebuilt in the 1980s and remains a pilgrimage site symbolizing the ancient origins of Tibetan kingship and the deep spiritual connection between the Tibetan people and their mountainous homeland.
Jokhang Temple
+1 [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. Great Works from other Civilizations provide +3 [ICON_PEACE] Faith.
[NEWLINE]"The Jokhang is the spiritual heart of Tibet, where the faithful come to touch the sacred."[NEWLINE] - Traditional Tibetan Saying[NEWLINE]

The Jokhang Temple, built in the 7th century CE, stands as the most sacred and important temple in Tibetan Buddhism. Located in the heart of Lhasa, it was commissioned by King Songtsen Gampo to house the precious Jowo Shakyamuni Buddha statue brought to Tibet by his Chinese wife, Princess Wencheng. The temple's name means "House of the Lord" and it has been the spiritual center of Tibet for over 1,300 years.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Jokhang represents a unique fusion of architectural styles, incorporating Tibetan, Chinese, Nepalese, and Indian influences, reflecting the diverse cultural exchanges that shaped early Tibetan Buddhism. Pilgrims from across the Tibetan plateau journey here to circumambulate the temple, prostrate before the sacred statue, and receive blessings. The temple complex includes numerous chapels housing important Buddhist relics and serves as the terminus of the sacred kora (circumambulation route) around Lhasa. Its significance extends beyond religion, as it has been a center of learning, cultural exchange, and political authority throughout Tibetan history.
Samye Monastery
+2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith. Religious Units gain +1 [ICON_MOVES] Movement. +1 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] GPP towards Great Engineers.
[NEWLINE]"Here was built the first monastery, where Buddhism took root in the Land of Snows."[NEWLINE] - From the Blue Annals[NEWLINE]

Samye Monastery, completed around 779 CE, holds the distinction of being the first Buddhist monastery built in Tibet. Founded during the reign of King Trisong Detsen, it was designed by the Indian master Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche) and built under the supervision of Shantarakshita. The monastery's unique architectural plan mirrors the Buddhist cosmological universe, with the main temple representing Mount Meru at the center, surrounded by smaller temples representing continents and subcontinents.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Samye played a crucial role in establishing Buddhism in Tibet and became the site of the famous debate between Indian and Chinese Buddhist schools, known as the Council of Samye. The monastery served as a major center of learning and translation, where Indian Buddhist texts were rendered into Tibetan. Its establishment marked the beginning of the systematic introduction of Buddhism to Tibet and the development of a distinctly Tibetan form of Buddhist practice. The monastery's influence extended far beyond its walls, as many of Tibet's most important religious figures studied and taught here, spreading Buddhist teachings throughout the Tibetan plateau.
Sakya Great Library
+2 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science. +1 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] GPP towards Great Scientists. Contains 2 slots for Great Works of Writing.
[NEWLINE]"Knowledge is the light that dispels the darkness of ignorance."[NEWLINE] - Sakya Pandita[NEWLINE]

The Great Library of Sakya Monastery, established in the 13th century, represents one of the world's most remarkable repositories of Buddhist knowledge and Tibetan culture. Founded as part of the Sakya school of Tibetan Buddhism, the library contains an extraordinary collection of over 84,000 scrolls, manuscripts, and texts covering Buddhism, medicine, astronomy, literature, and history. Many of these works are written on palm leaves and birch bark, some dating back over 1,000 years.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The library's collection includes rare Sanskrit manuscripts, original Tibetan translations of Buddhist sutras, and unique works on Tibetan medicine and astrology. During the Yuan Dynasty, when Sakya lamas served as spiritual advisors to the Mongol emperors, the monastery became a major center of learning that attracted scholars from across Asia. The systematic preservation and cataloging of knowledge at Sakya contributed significantly to the preservation of Buddhist philosophy and Tibetan intellectual traditions. Today, the library remains an invaluable resource for understanding the development of Tibetan Buddhism and the broader cultural exchanges between Tibet, India, China, and Mongolia throughout history.
Potala Palace
Defense Points for each religious follower in Cities. +2 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] GPP towards Great Engineers.[NEWLINE]Must be built on a Mountain.
[NEWLINE]"A palace that rises to touch the heavens, home to the living Buddha."[NEWLINE] - Tibetan Pilgrimage Song[NEWLINE]

The Potala Palace, towering majestically over Lhasa at 3,700 meters above sea level, stands as the architectural masterpiece of Tibet and former seat of the Dalai Lamas. Construction began in 1645 under the Fifth Dalai Lama and took nearly 50 years to complete. The palace contains over 1,000 rooms, including the tombs of eight Dalai Lamas, numerous chapels, and vast libraries containing sacred texts and artifacts.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Rising 13 stories and measuring 400 meters east-west and 350 meters north-south, the Potala Palace represents the pinnacle of Tibetan architecture and engineering. The White Palace served as the administrative quarters and living quarters of the Dalai Lama, while the Red Palace housed the sacred chapels and stupas. The palace served as the center of Tibetan political and religious authority for over 300 years, hosting important ceremonies and serving as a pilgrimage destination. Its massive walls, built without mortar using a technique called "rammed earth," have withstood centuries of earthquakes. The palace's design incorporates both defensive features and spiritual symbolism, representing the earthly residence of Avalokiteshvara, the bodhisattva of compassion.
Norbulingka
+3 [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness. Gardens have doubled efficacy.[NEWLINE]Must be built next to a River.
[NEWLINE]"In summer's embrace, the Jewel Park blooms with earthly paradise."[NEWLINE] - From the Songs of the Seventh Dalai Lama[NEWLINE]

Norbulingka, meaning "Jewel Park," served as the summer palace of the Dalai Lamas from the 1780s until 1959. Located on the outskirts of Lhasa, this 36-hectare complex represents the largest man-made garden in Tibet and exemplifies the pinnacle of Tibetan landscape architecture. The Seventh Dalai Lama began its construction as a retreat from the formal constraints of the Potala Palace, creating a space where nature and architecture harmoniously blend.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The palace complex contains several buildings connected by tree-lined paths and surrounded by meticulously maintained gardens featuring over 100 varieties of plants, many rare in Tibet's high-altitude environment. The gardens include traditional Tibetan medicinal plants, ornamental flowers, and fruit trees, creating microclimates that support diverse flora. Norbulingka served as more than just a residence; it was a center of Tibetan arts and culture, hosting opera performances, religious festivals, and important political meetings. The palace's design philosophy emphasizes harmony with nature, featuring pavilions that frame mountain views and water features that reflect the sky. During the summer months, the entire Tibetan government would relocate here, making it effectively the seasonal capital of Tibet.
Gyantse Kumbum
+3 [ICON_GOLD] Gold. Contains 3 slots for Great Works of Art. Theming Bonus for works from Different Eras.
[NEWLINE]"Within these walls, ten thousand Buddhas smile upon the faithful."[NEWLINE] - Inscription at Gyantse Kumbum[NEWLINE]

The Gyantse Kumbum, built in the early 15th century, stands as one of Tibet's most remarkable architectural and artistic achievements. This multi-story chorten (stupa) contains 75 chapels arranged across nine levels, housing what is considered the finest collection of Tibetan Buddhist art under one roof. The word "Kumbum" means "100,000 images," referring to the countless murals, sculptures, and mandalas that adorn its interior spaces.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Constructed as part of the Palcho Monastery complex, the Kumbum represents a unique architectural form that combines Indian stupa design with Tibetan and Nepalese influences. Each level is dedicated to different aspects of Buddhist teaching, with artwork representing various schools of Tibetan Buddhism. The murals, painted by Newar artists from Nepal and local Tibetan masters, showcase a synthesis of artistic traditions spanning from the 15th to 18th centuries. The Kumbum's design allows pilgrims to follow a prescribed route through all levels, encountering different meditation practices and teachings along the way. This architectural mandala serves both as an art gallery and a three-dimensional guide to Buddhist cosmology, making it one of the most important repositories of Himalayan Buddhist art and culture.
Dégé Parkhang
Bonus Religious Pressure and Range per Great Work of Writing in the City. Contains 2 slots for Great Works of Writing. +2 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] GPP towards Great Writers.
[NEWLINE]"From these blocks of wood, the wisdom of ages flows like water from a spring."[NEWLINE] - Dégé Printing House Motto[NEWLINE]

The Dégé Parkhang, established in 1729, represents the most important printing house in Tibetan history and remains the largest repository of Tibetan woodblock printing in the world. Located in Dégé County in eastern Tibet, this remarkable institution houses over 320,000 printing blocks and has produced millions of texts over nearly three centuries. The printing house was founded by the kings of Dégé as part of their effort to preserve and disseminate Tibetan Buddhist culture and learning.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Parkhang's collection includes virtually the entire Tibetan Buddhist canon, including the Kangyur (Buddha's teachings) and Tengyur (commentaries), as well as works on medicine, astronomy, literature, and history. The traditional printing process using hand-carved wooden blocks and handmade paper continues today much as it has for centuries. Master craftsmen carve text in mirror image onto birch wood blocks, which are then used to print on traditional Tibetan paper made from local plants. The printing house has played a crucial role in standardizing Tibetan script and preserving texts that might otherwise have been lost. During times of political upheaval, the Parkhang served as a vital center for maintaining Tibetan cultural identity and religious practice, earning it recognition as the "Vatican" of Tibetan Buddhism.
To maximize your bonus, make sure this building contains Great Works of Art from 3 different eras.
